title: Add lightweight RAG stub runtime and interactive toolchain debugger quickstart
author: Nikhil Suresh
description: Context: Engineers repeatedly ask for a small, reproducible RAG quickstart that makes it easy to iterate on prompt/tool-call logic locally and to debug the sequence of tool invocations. Existing examples demonstrate production runtimes or full orchestration but are heavy for local experimentation. This PR introduces a lightweight 'rag-stub' runtime and an interactive 'toolchain-debugger' that replays a request end-to-end and lets you step through prompt transforms, tool calls, KV-cache behavior, and streaming tokens. Motivation: faster dev loop for integrators and DEx teams; lower friction for writing and validating tool bindings across TypeScript and Python. What this PR adds (summary): - examples/rag-stub/: a self-contained quickstart that runs with a single docker-compose command or via devcontainer. - rag-stub runtime: tiny express-based stub that simulates prefix caching, continuous-batching semantics, and streaming chunks so UI and SDKs can be exercised. - toolchain-debugger: a small web UI (TS) that connects to the stub runtime and provides step-through execution, state snapshots, and prompt diffing. - typed tool bindings: TS and Python example bindings showing best-practices for tool input schemas, validation, and structured output parsing. - Devcontainer and small CI smoke test to run the quickstart on GitHub Actions (linux matrix + node/python checks). - Docs update: docs/how-tos/rag/debugging-toolchains.md linking to the quickstart and describing common debugging workflows. Checklist: - [x] Design and RFC reviewed (ENG-4128) - [x] Core implementation: runtime + UI + bindings - [x] Unit tests for tool binding helpers - [x] Integration smoke test in CI - [x] Devcontainer and local run instructions - [x] Docs page with step-through walkthrough - [x] TypeScript and Python package manifest and lints Passing CI: initial run had lint/type failures; fixed in follow-up commits. Scope notes: this is intentionally minimal (no real model weights or full KV store); the stub simulates timings and KV responses so developers can reproduce timing-sensitive regressions. The quickstart is meant for local development, examples, and onboarding — not for production use. Implementation details (high level): - rag-stub/runtime/index.js: Express server, endpoints: /generate (accepts prompt, returns streaming chunks), /cache (simulated KV get/put), /replay (replay session traces). - toolchain-debugger/src/: React + small state machine that connects to /replay and renders a timeline of prompt transformations and tool results; step forward/back facilities and diff view. - ts/ and py/ bindings demonstrate how to wire Redwood SDK calls to tool implementations and how to serialize/deserialize structured outputs. - CI: .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml runs the devcontainer in headless mode and executes a scripted session to ensure the runtime and bindings launch. Migration notes: none for production consumers; examples consumers should follow docs/how-tos for local setup. Related work: complements the existing RAG quickstarts by providing an interactive debugging surface that was repeatedly requested in onboarding feedback. Rollout: merged to main, will be linked from the public examples index and docs site.

Diego: requested stronger type exports for the TS bindings and an additional unit test for prompt sanitizer; action: added named exports and tests. Samira (UX): requested keyboard stepper and improved diffing; action: added step keyboard bindings and a compact unified diff view. CI initially failed due to ESLint rule 'no-explicit-any' in TS bindings — fixed, re-ran, green. Final approvals from Claire and Diego on 2025-12-03; merged on 2025-12-04 using squash merge.
release_notes: Adds a local RAG quickstart with a lightweight stub runtime and an interactive toolchain debugger for step-through inspection of prompt transforms and tool calls. Includes TypeScript and Python bindings, devcontainer, and CI smoke test. Intended for developer onboarding and local debugging (not production).
